t: Electronic Circuit Designer - Signature build-tool concept
title: Electronic Circuit Designer - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Creates circuit schematics from electrical requirements.
description:
The Signature Electronic Circuit Designer exists to creates circuit schematics from electrical requirements. It is one of the fundamental capabilities in the AI build-tool catalog: the set of tools, engines and disciplines an AI needs to design, engineer, generate, test and deliver things on demand. Where public tools each solve a slice of the problem, the Signature line defines the whole capability as a coherent framework with contracts between its parts.

Consider what happens without a disciplined Electronic Circuit Designer. Electronic Circuit Designer work degrades into folklore - tricks that work on one machine, steps remembered differently by every practitioner, failures nobody can reproduce. The Signature framework answers with determinism: declared inputs, explicit transformations, verified outputs, and an audit trail that explains every result. The pillars below are the machinery that makes that promise concrete.

This is a Signature-concept database: the framework it describes is the Signature line's own design, labeled as such throughout. The techniques and standards records cite real public knowledge; the pillars and drills are the Signature system's original construction. All of it ships with runnable demos, because in the Signature line a tool proves itself by running.

t: Signature Calculator - Electronic Circuit Designer framework pillar
title: Signature Calculator - Electronic Circuit Designer framework pillar
definition: The Calculator component of the Signature Electronic Circuit Designer framework, owning calculator. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature Electronic Circuit Designer framework, the Calculator owns the framework's calculator responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Calculator's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Calculator from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. Every execution is checked against the charter (Creates circuit schematics from electrical requirements.). If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Walk through it concretely. A Electronics and embedded systems build needs Electronic Circuit Designer, so the framework invokes the Calculator on the the framework's calculator responsibilities portion of the work. The demo program attached to this record executes the pillar's essential algorithm on sample data - run it with node and watch each step print its reasoning. Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Electronic Circuit Designer. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Draftsman - Electronic Circuit Designer framework pillar
title: Signature Draftsman - Electronic Circuit Designer framework pillar
definition: The Draftsman component of the Signature Electronic Circuit Designer framework, owning draftsman. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature Electronic Circuit Designer framework decomposes the capability (Creates circuit schematics from electrical requirements.) into seven pillars, and the Draftsman is the one that owns the framework's draftsman responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a Electronic Circuit Designer result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Draftsman's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Draftsman's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for Electronic Circuit Designer. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Placer - Electronic Circuit Designer framework pillar
title: Signature Placer - Electronic Circuit Designer framework pillar
definition: The Placer component of the Signature Electronic Circuit Designer framework, owning placer. Signature concept.
description:
The Placer is a load-bearing component of the Signature Electronic Circuit Designer framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's placer responsibilities belongs to the Placer, and the Placer answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Placer can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Placer works like this. A build request arrives carrying the Electronic Circuit Designer charter (creates circuit schematics from electrical requirements.). The Placer reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for an small electronics job that needs Electronic Circuit Designer. The Placer takes the request's placer responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Placer's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.
